name: Kit
summary: Email marketing built for creators (formerly ConvertKit). Grow your list with landing pages and forms, then automate newsletters and sell digital products from one place; a beta Kit MCP connects AI assistants like Claude directly to your account. Recent additions: a new landing-page editor, Dynamic Content, Newsletter Sponsorships, and App Store integrations on paid plans — SMS via SlickText, Patreon member sync (tier and support data in automations), Luma/Eventbrite event sync, and two-way HubSpot CRM sync on Pro.
best_for: creators, writers and coaches building an audience-first business who want email, landing pages, digital products and a creator network in one
skip_if: you're an e-commerce store (commerce-native email tools fit better) or your list is big-but-cold — clean it before paying per subscriber
honest_knock: Three honest notes. Subscriber-based pricing counts everyone on your list — cold subscribers cost the same as fans, so prune before you price. The free plan changed shape in 2026: it now runs to 10,000 subscribers rather than 1,000 (re-verified 2026-09-02), but Visual Automations and email sequences came out of it, so the free tier sends and captures without automating anything — what puts you on Creator at $39/mo, or $33/mo paid yearly, is wanting a welcome sequence rather than list growth. And the 35% price hike in 2025 changed the value math: the free tier is still arguably the best in creator email, but paid tiers now deserve comparison shopping rather than default loyalty. The creator-first features (tip jars, paid newsletters, recommendations) remain the real differentiator.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-02) The free plan is $0/mo and covers up to 10,000 email subscribers, with unlimited landing pages and forms, unlimited email broadcasts, audience tagging and segmentation, and digital products and subscriptions. Kit renamed the old Newsletter plan to Free and took automation out of it: Visual Automations and email sequences are now Creator-and-above, and Kit's affiliate briefing of 2 September 2026 adds that new free accounts open with a 14-day Creator trial and that accounts already on the Newsletter plan keep what they had. Creator is $39/mo billed monthly, or $33/mo billed yearly ($390 a year, saving $78), and adds unlimited Visual Automations, unlimited email sequences, Kit MCP, SMS marketing and branding removal. Pro — the tier that adds Subscriber Signals, engagement analytics, deliverability reporting, a newsletter referral system and unlimited users — is $79/mo billed monthly, or $66/mo billed yearly ($790 a year, saving $158). Paying yearly saves 17%. Every paid price on the page is quoted for 1,000 email subscribers and Kit bills by list size, so read the tier for your own list before you budget. Paid plans open with a 14-day free trial without a card, and migrations are free. Read again on 9 October 2026 with the slider, step by step. Creator billed monthly: $39 up to 1,000, $59 up to 3,000, $89 up to 5,000, $119 up to 8,000, $139 up to 10,000, $169 up to 15,000, $189 up to 20,000, $199 up to 25,000, $259 up to 35,000, $319 up to 45,000, $379 up to 55,000, $439 up to 65,000, $499 up to 75,000, $559 up to 85,000, $619 up to 95,000, $679 up to 105,000 subscribers; billed yearly, per month, at the same steps: $33, $50, $75, $100, $116, $141, $158, $166, $216, $266, $316, $366, $416, $466, $516, $566. Pro billed monthly at the same steps: $79, $99, $139, $169, $189, $249, $269, $279, $363, $447, $519, $591, $663, $735, $807, $879; billed yearly, per month: $66, $83, $116, $141, $158, $208, $225, $233, $303, $373, $433, $493, $553, $613, $673, $733. The page carried a 'LIMITED TIME PRO OFFER' banner on that reading; read again on 10 October 2026, the yearly view spells it out as an extra 25% off the first year of Pro billed yearly: $50/mo instead of $66, or $593 for the first year at 1,000 subscribers, and the plan renews at the standard rate after that first year. Creator showed no offer and stayed at $33/mo billed yearly ($390). Re-read 15 October 2026 at 1,000 subscribers in the default yearly view: unchanged, with Creator at $33/mo ($390 a year) and the Pro first-year offer still running at $50/mo ($593 for the first year, against $66/mo standard); the page's 'save $355 first year' is measured against twelve monthly payments of $79 ($948), and against the standard yearly $790 the saving is $197.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the 14-day trial of the Creator plan (not the Free plan), without entering a card and without sending anything: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported three made-up subscribers with tags from a CSV file, exported them, and re-imported a changed file with one new name and one empty name cell.
findings: The CSV importer did not map a single column on its own, not even 'email'; we mapped email, first name and tags by hand. Step 3 adds an import tag by default ('Imported October 23rd, 2026 at 10:42 PM'), and the import finished with '3 subscribers processed'.
All three imported subscribers were 'Confirmed' straight away, although no opt-in email was sent. The 'Total subscribers' statistic stayed at 0 while the list itself showed 'Total: 3'.

Re-importing on the same email addresses created no duplicates and took over the changed name, but an empty first-name cell erased the existing name of that subscriber. Clean your file before a re-import: a blank cell is not ignored.

Export (select all > ... > Export) put a download link in the Notifications menu within a few seconds: a CSV with 14 columns, and all three subscribers came back with name and tags, including the automatic import tag.

Right after the five onboarding questions, a window opened with card fields and 'Subscribe to the Creator Plan', with the yearly plan ($390) preselected over monthly ($39). It closes with the cross, and the trial then runs without a card ('14 / 14 days remaining in trial'). The website field had been prefilled with the domain of our email address.
